headline: Highest risk is data leakage: cognee handles personal/finance/support data while EMQX has broad egress, creating a plausible default exfiltration path; other risks are moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not provably present. However, cognee can process documents and workflows, and EMQX exposes an HTTP API with broad egress, so if outputs are bridged manually or via files, injected content could influence downstream behavior. This is a low-severity, configuration-dependent pathway.
conditions: IF outputs from cognee are copied into EMQX-managed content or messages
IF an operator uses a shared file or clipboard bridge between the two agents
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Disable any copy-paste or file-based handoff between agents
Add a human review step before forwarding cognee outputs
Use content sanitization for any bridged text

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while EMQX has broad network egress and touches IoT data. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair creates a plausible default leakage path if cognee outputs are forwarded into EMQX or its HTTP API. The blast radius includes sensitive data, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF cognee outputs containing personal or finance data are sent to EMQX
IF EMQX forwards received payloads to external services or logs them
mitigations: Restrict forwarded fields to non-sensitive summaries
Block sensitive classes from any EMQX payloads
Review HTTP API logging settings
Use separate credentials and tenants
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering before transmission

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can operate concurrently, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git state, or mutable resource. cognee is CLI-based with session memory, and EMQX exposes an HTTP API; absent a shared writable target, direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains, so low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mutable backend
IF a shared HTTP resource or database is introduced
mitigations: Assign separate storage namespaces
Avoid shared mutable resources
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Document ownership of each backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, which EMQX could consume if an operator forwards outputs into its HTTP API. EMQX is not documented as critically evaluating those inputs, so A-to-B propagation could turn an upstream mistake into an operational action or stored message. The pathway exists by inference, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF EMQX treats cognee-generated content as authoritative input
IF downstream automation acts on forwarded decisions or workflows
mitigations: Require manual verification before forwarding outputs
Add schema validation on incoming payloads
Limit EMQX actions to read-only processing
Log provenance for each forwarded item

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while EMQX touches IoT data and has broad egress. If regulated personal or financial data is routed into EMQX without a matching compliance posture, retention or residency mismatches can create a breach. The profiles do not show certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF personal or finance data from cognee is routed through EMQX
IF EMQX retention or residency differs from the source policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing
Exclude regulated fields from EMQX traffic
Check retention settings on both systems
Document residency and deletion handling
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both agents
